title: Danish Rye Bread
subtitle: Dense, seedy Scandinavian rye loaf
excerpt: A thick, heavy batter of dark rye flour, caraway seeds, and honey is mixed, rested overnight, and baked into a dense, moist loaf. Danish rugbrod is eaten every day in Denmark as the base for open sandwiches. It contains no yeast -- only time and rye flour do the work.
sourceNotes: Danish rugbrod is a dense, moist rye bread. It is eaten every day in Denmark as the base for smorrebrod (open sandwiches). It contains no sugar and very little fat -- its flavour comes from the rye and a long rest.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: This bread needs an overnight rest after mixing. Slice the next day -- it cuts much better when completely cold.

content.text: Rye bread dough is more like a very thick batter than a traditional bread dough -- it cannot be kneaded. Mix it well, press it into the loaf tin, and leave it overnight. The long rest is not optional. It develops flavour and changes the texture of the crumb.

items.prepNote: use dark rye flour -- not plain wheat flour

content.text: Mix rye flour, baking powder, salt, and caraway seeds in a large bowl.
Add warm milk, honey, and sunflower oil. Mix to a thick, heavy batter -- this is not a kneadable dough. It will look quite wet.
Pour into a greased 900g loaf tin. Smooth the top with a wet spoon. Cover with a clean cloth and leave to rest at room temperature overnight (8 hours minimum).
Bake at 180°C for 55-60 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.
Leave in the tin for 10 minutes then cool completely on a rack before slicing -- this takes at least 2 hours.

items.symptom: Loaf is sticky inside after baking
items.cause: Not baked long enough or not cooled
items.fix: Leave in the tin for 10 minutes then cool on a rack for at least 2 hours before slicing.

content.text: Denmark. Eaten every day. The base of the open sandwich (smorrebrod). Danes eat more rye per person than almost any other country. The bread keeps well for up to a week, improving slightly as it firms up.
